title: Growing onion microgreens
subtitle: Grass-like allium shoots with a mild onion flavour, cut in 14 to 21 days
excerpt: Onion microgreens grow as narrow, hollow green shoots with a mild raw-onion flavour. The cycle is 14 to 21 days, similar to leek. Sow densely, blackout for four days, then grow in good light until the shoots reach 10 to 12 cm.
sourceNotes: UMass Extension microgreens guides (open-access). Cornell Cooperative Extension indoor growing material. Standard microgreen-growing practice synthesised from extension service material.

glossaryTerms.definition: Watering by setting the growing tray inside a second tray filled with water, allowing the growing medium to draw moisture up from below. Keeps the seedling surface dry and reduces mould and damping-off risk in microgreen trays.

A fungal condition where seedling stems collapse and rot at the soil surface. Caused by Pythium, Fusarium, and Rhizoctonia species in warm, wet, poorly-ventilated conditions. Common in overcrowded or overwatered microgreen trays.

content.text: Onion microgreens grow as narrow, hollow grass-like shoots with a mild raw-onion flavour. The cycle is 14 to 21 days on a 25 cm indoor tray: sow, cover and blackout for four days, then bring to light and grow for the remaining 10 to 17 days until the shoots are 10 to 12 cm tall. The flavour is milder than mature spring onions but more persistent than chive microgreens.
Onion microgreens follow the same growing pattern as leek microgreens. The extended cycle means the main risk is mould on the medium surface during the long light phase; airflow is the key control.

Light: a south-facing windowsill in spring and summer. In winter a grow light 15 to 20 cm above the tray at 14 hours per day is needed for consistent results. Onion microgreens in low winter light develop slowly and produce very thin, pale stems.
Temperature: 18 to 22°C. Onion seed germinates poorly below 15°C; keep the tray in a consistently warm room throughout the growing period.

Day 0: sow. Fill the tray with pre-dampened seed compost to within 1 cm of the rim. Scatter onion microgreen seed at 20 to 30 g per 25 cm tray. The black angular seed is easy to distribute. Press gently into contact with the medium.

Days 1 to 4: blackout. Cover with a second tray, lightly weighted. Onion shoots emerge as U-shaped loops (the seed coat attached to the tip) before straightening; this is normal. Remove the cover once the majority have straightened to 2 to 3 cm.
Day 5 onward: light. The shoots green up over 24 to 48 hours in a bright position. Rotate the tray 180 degrees every two days for even stem straightness.

daily throughout the growing phase. Set the tray inside a second outer tray with 1 to 2 cm of water and allow the medium to absorb it. Remove excess water after 30 minutes to avoid standing water that encourages mould.

Days 14 to 21: cut. When the shoots are 10 to 12 cm tall and a consistent green throughout, cut 1 cm above the medium with scissors. Use fresh; onion microgreens do not keep as well as brassica cotyledons. Refrigerate in a sealed container for up to two days.

attrs.heading: Troubleshooting
attrs.intro: Common problems on onion microgreen trays.

items.symptom: Mould on the medium surface after the first week
items.cause: Prolonged damp period in a still, warm room.
items.fix: Run a small fan at low speed nearby. Bottom-water only and remove standing water from the outer tray after 30 minutes. The mould is on the substrate; the shoots remain safe.

items.cause: Old or coated seed, or cold room.
items.fix: Onion seed has a shorter viability window than brassica seed; use fresh stock. Aim for room temperature of 18°C or above.

items.cause: Insufficient light or one-directional light source.
items.fix: Add a grow light or move to a brighter position. Rotate the tray every two days to even out light exposure.

items.symptom: Shoots rot at base after day 7
items.cause: Damping off from excess moisture in medium.
items.fix: Remove standing water from the outer tray promptly. Discard affected tray and restart.

content.text: Onion seed viability declines after one to two years; test germination before committing to a full tray. Standard vegetable onion seed is usually untreated. Microgreen suppliers stock onion seed in appropriate pack sizes.
risk is higher on allium trays than on fast brassica trays because of the longer growing window. Consistent airflow and bottom-watering are the controls.
